statements.quote: Data confidentiality was strictly maintained, with anonymised identifiers and secure storage on encrypted drives.
statements.locator: p. 5, Section 3.1 Design and participants, consent/confidentiality paragraph

statements.quote: These assessments were based on authentic outputs such as notated scores, improvisation recordings, and written analyses.
statements.locator: p. 5, Section 3.2 Research context, weekly assessments paragraph

statements.quote: Every two weeks, students submitted both a creative product (e.g., a composition or improvisation) and an accompanying analytical task (e.g., harmonic labeling or structural justification), which were collected through a secure digital submission platform. In addition to these, participants in the experimental group were required to share a screenshot of their interaction with ChatGPT or a link to such interaction.

All submissions were anonymized before being evaluated by independent raters using the calibrated rubrics described earlier. Data from the 12 time points were then compiled into longitudinal datasets for subsequent statistical analysis.
statements.locator: p. 8, Section 3.6 Procedure, continuation at top of page

statements.quote: Several analyses were employed to address the research questions using SPSS (version 26), R (version 4.3.1), Epistemic Network Analysis (ENA) Lab (https://www.epistemicnetwork.org/), and Python (version 3.13.7).
statements.locator: p. 8, Section 3.7 Analysis, first paragraph; ENA software homepage

notes:
Checked on 2026-10-09 using Python urllib with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1, without credentials or personal identifiers. Read the entire 98175-character markdown in seven consecutive chunks, including all references through p. 19. Checked PDF text with PyMuPDF at pp. 5, 7, 8, and 17 and scanned all PDF pages for availability/repository/supplement/preregistration terms. The version of record is Thinking Skills and Creativity 63 (2027), article 102344, available online 23 August 2026; DOI 10.1016/j.tsc.2026.102344.

The explicit data-availability statement on p. 17 says the data are available on request from the corresponding author. No study repository, public code release, preregistration, supplementary-file link, or appendix is identified in this document. The form's data_and_code contains an on-request description and an empty code_url, with no URLs. Statements include the availability declaration and relevant data-handling, output-collection, software, and data-curation passages. Quotes preserve PDF wording and punctuation, with line breaks normalized to spaces.

No deposit belonging to c148 was confirmed, so deposits is empty. The ENA homepage named in Section 3.7 returned HTTP 200 and describes general analysis software; it is not this study's data/code deposit. Unrelated repositories/publications returned by searches are not counted as c148 deposits. No participant-level data file was available to inspect; no rows, columns, assignment fields, outcomes, texts, or data license could be confirmed. No authors were contacted.

Publisher limitation: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tsc.2026.102344 returned HTTP 302 followed by HTTP 200 at https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S187118712600218X, which was an HTML page titled 'Redirecting', not the article/supplement listing. The direct landing page https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S187118712600218X returned HTTP 403. Consequently, the absence of publisher-hosted supplementary data cannot be independently verified. The journal homepage redirected (HTTP 307) to ScienceDirect and returned HTTP 403. No login, account, access request, CAPTCHA solution, or bot-check bypass was attempted.

Search limitations: the very broad DataCite name/keyword searches and Zenodo name/keyword searches were screened only through their returned first pages; the narrower title, creator/topic, ORCID, and DOI searches are recorded separately. The OSF first-author query used the title filter required by the brief, not a full contributor-name index. Zenodo initially rejected size=100 with HTTP 400; size=25 worked without authentication. One additional short-title Zenodo request timed out and is recorded with n_results null. Repeated requests for the same query are consolidated. Overall confidence is medium because of these search limits and the unavailable publisher supplement listing; the explicit on-request declaration itself is directly verified.

No public data currently resolve final.open_items. In particular, participant-level arm SDs and class identifiers (open_questions[6]) and class counts/class-adjusted precision (open_questions[0]) remain unavailable; per-person means, SDs, SEs, and analyzed counts cannot be recomputed or verified from a public dataset. The MANCOVA outcome definition, assessment timing, prior-arm crosswalk, scoring/rater aggregation and reliability, and disputed model output also remain unresolved. Participant-linked notated scores, recordings, written analyses, and interaction logs were described as collected, but no public release was found from which diversity measures could be calculated.
